title: [skill] pm-dispatch: semantic-ruling template must carry a compiler-face checklist — process half of the #5930 ruling
body:
Follow-up filed from the 2026-08-07 maintainer ruling on #5930 (decision batch accepted via the PM session). Unclaimed; no labels applied — routing belongs to the triage seat (landing site is `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` ⇒ devx per the domain table's `skills/**` row… flagged, not self-applied).

## Ruling context

#5930 measured that one `FilterCondition` semantics is implemented by 5 mutually independent compilers/evaluators, so every semantic ruling costs ×5 and misses recur (#5146 missed face 2 → became #5903; #5326/#5335 each spent a lap re-aligning faces 3/4). The maintainer ruled: the lowering-layer convergence investigation goes `pm:on-hold` (restart condition recorded on #5930); the **process half lands now** — this card.

## Scope

Add to the pm-dispatch SKILL, in the dispatch-prompt guidance (step 5 area), a standing clause:

- Every **filter/predicate semantic ruling** dispatched for implementation must enumerate the full compiler-face checklist in the dispatch prompt, and the dev's PR must state per face: changed / already conformant / explicitly out of scope (with reason).
- The five faces as of today (from #5930): driver-sql (`sql-driver.ts`, inherited by wasm/turso-local), turso RemoteTransport (`buildWhereSQL`), service-analytics read-scope-sql, service-analytics filter-normalizer, formula `matchesFilterCondition`. Plus the half-face: objectql `having-filter.ts` (#5905). driver-memory/mongodb: frozen, pin-annotate instead of flip (#5499).
- Model text: #5298 §1's cost inventory is the reference shape.

## Acceptance

- SKILL.md carries the clause with the face list and the "per face: changed / conformant / out-of-scope" reporting requirement.
- The clause notes the list itself is maintained by PR when faces are added/removed (same discipline as the domain table).

Refs: #5930 (ruling + hold record), #5298 §1 (model), #5903 / #5905 (misses this clause prevents).
